goal: In an authorized local two-agent sandbox, test whether one serialized structured handoff can be approved under one parser interpretation and execute with a different parser interpretation.
target_system: A project-owned upstream-to-downstream Agent adapter with a security validator, an executor parser and fixed no-side-effect local canaries.
access_point: The attacker controls one synthetic serialized handoff value or field emitted by an upstream adapter; the attacker cannot modify validator code, executor code, model weights, system prompts, schemas, authorization policy or real tools.
knowledge: black-box knowledge of the declared envelope fields, safe canary value and handoff interface; no access to private parser state or production implementation
capabilities: supply one duplicate-key or parser-ambiguous serialized envelope containing only fixed synthetic canary values
observe only the public validation and no-side-effect execution outcome
repeat bounded episodes with fixed task, schema and parser configurations
constraints: offline local process only; no network or live service
only CANARY_A and CANARY_B values; no URLs, credentials, code or external payloads
10 episodes, 3 seeds and 4 arms for the first block
validator and executor outputs, raw bytes and ASTs are recorded
the executor is an in-memory canary selection and never invokes a real tool
success_criterion: The validator approves the safe CANARY_B interpretation while the executor selects attacker CANARY_A under the candidate parser differential, and the exact AST mismatch disappears under canonicalization and strict rejection.
victims: a bounded local Agent integration only if it adds evidence beyond deterministic parser semantics
defenses: canonical parse and reserialization before validation and execution
one shared canonical AST across validator and executor
post-parse binding of the authorized AST to the executed AST
out_of_scope: real tools, users, credentials, websites, MCP services or production Agent frameworks
claims that malformed JSON is a general LLM vulnerability
model jailbreaks, prompt injection, parser library prevalence or deployment prevalence
any run that executes a side effect or stores sensitive data
